query: How do I change a flat tyre on a car?
answer:
First, get somewhere safe. Pull onto flat, solid ground well away from traffic, turn on your hazard lights and apply the parking brake. If you have wheel chocks, or a heavy rock, wedge them against the wheel diagonally opposite the flat so the car can't roll [1][2]. Take out the spare, the jack and the wheel brace (lug wrench). Remove any hubcap, then loosen each wheel nut about half a turn while the tyre is still on the ground. Don't take them off yet [1][3].

Put the jack under the jacking point shown in your owner's manual, because the wrong spot can damage the car. Raise the car just until the flat tyre clears the ground, and never put any part of your body under a car that's held up only by a jack [1][2]. Remove the nuts, pull the wheel straight off and fit the spare by lining its holes up with the studs. Tighten the nuts by hand, then snug them with the brace in a star (criss-cross) pattern without overtightening [2][3]. Lower the car fully, then tighten the nuts firmly in the same star pattern and check the spare's pressure [1][3].

Afterwards, many temporary "space-saver" spares have a lower speed and distance limit, which is printed on the tyre or in the manual. Get the flat repaired or replaced soon, and have the wheel nuts checked or torqued to the correct spec [2][3]. If your car has no spare and only a sealant kit, or the spot feels unsafe, call roadside assistance instead.
